title: Draw with image coordinates
summary: OpenCV drawing points use x, y order. x is the column and y is the row. A negative thickness can fill a shape.
introduction: OpenCV drawing points use x, y order. x is the column and y is the row. A negative thickness can fill a shape. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: OpenCV drawing points use x, y order. x is the column and y is the row. A negative thickness can fill a shape.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

image = np.zeros((5, 5, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
cv2.rectangle(image, (1, 1), (3, 3), (0, 255, 0), thickness=-1)
print(image[2, 2].tolist(), image[0, 0].tolist())
blocks.title: Draw with image coordinates

blocks.text: The centre pixel is [0, 255, 0], which is green in BGR. The corner pixel remains [0, 0, 0]. The rectangle fills the selected area.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Array indexing is row, column, but drawing points are x, y.
For more detail later, use this [OpenCV further reading](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/d00/tutorial_py_root.html).
